notes.body: Here are the other warnings detected by this check.  Is it worth enabling these warnings and setting these long help / blurb fields to NULL?  I wonder how many of these were set by someone who didn't realise they could set to NULL and didn't want to fall foul of the pre-commit check?[blurb_warnings.txt](/uploads/2c7dd555c08512c6da5ecaadfb3ba555/blurb_warnings.txt)

@alagoutte  - what do you think?  Is it worth getting rid of most/all of these to save a few KB and set a better example?

See also the check in the script - it could check for the exact pattern you saw (protname + <label-words>).  Could achieve this by telling it the protocol name, or maybe just doing split('.')[0] on that item's filter?  I don't know how common that pattern would be.
It is recommanded if remember ? (on some doc) for don't use the same stuff)

If it's not to much work cleaning it up would be good IMHO.

skrev:

Its enforced by one of the perl pre-commit scripts that they aren't identical.  Not sure if comparison is case-sensitive or not.

But I'm seeing cases where the same words are just given in a different order, and also cases where the blurb is a subset of the label words, which I think we can say is not adding anything, i.e. NULL (so default to same value as label) would be better.
I've changed quite a few long texts to NULL.  Will wait to see if anyone objects before merging this or doing any more.
